title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'troisième mouture' of Analysis situs (1986), Grothendieck is testing an axiomatic formalism. A space is given by a set or poset of 'liens', which are compact contractible pieces. These pieces carry a lattice of 'ouverts', a structure in which sup is not set-theoretic union. They also carry a 'support' map A ↦ |A| into an underlying point set. The previous page found a candidate counterexample, the 'ficelle à deux brins': two arcs from 0 to 1, topologically a circle. Its liens are indexed by pairs (x,x') with x in the open first strand and x' in the open second strand, i.e. by I°×I°.

This page generalises the example and analyses it. Let I, I' be totally ordered sets, each with a smallest element 0 and a largest element 1; these are the 'trucs à extrémités'. Form J = I°×I' ° with the product partial order, adjoin a global minimum 0 and maximum 1, and write J° = I°×I'°.

For z = (x,x') in J°, the singleton A_z = {z} is declared open. The justification is that it is the complement of the union of the 'droites' [z'',1] for z''>z and [0,z'] for z'<z. Its complement is written B_z = {z' : z'<z or z'>z}, i.e. Grothendieck tacitly restricts to the elements comparable with z.

The natural support map takes values in I ⊔ I' (glued at 0 and 1). It is |z| = {x,x'}, |0| = {0}, |1| = {1}. One then checks that |B_z| is the complement of |z|, as it should be.

Now take z1 = (x1,x1') and z2 = (x2,x2') incomparable, with x1<x2 in I and x2'<x1' in I'. Then:
- |B_{z1} ∩ B_{z2}| ⊊ |B_{z1}| ∩ |B_{z2}|. What is missing is ]x1,x2[ on I and ]x2',x1'[ on I'.
- |A_{z1} ∨ A_{z2}| = [x1,x2] ∪ [x2',x1'] ⊋ |A_{z1}| ∪ |A_{z2}| = {x1,x2,x1',x2'}.

So supports commute neither with inf (∩) nor with sup (∨) in the lattice of opens.

The next page completes the analysis. It takes z3 = (x3,x3') with x3 between x1 and x2 and x3' between x2' and x1'. Then A_{z3} ∧ (A_{z1} ∨ A_{z2}) = A_{z3}, but (A_{z3} ∧ A_{z1}) ∨ (A_{z3} ∧ A_{z2}) = ∅. Hence the lattice of opens is not distributive (Grothendieck says 'not modular'; see errors). The Scholie concludes that the support formalism is fine provided one does not compare supports of strata and of 'compatible figures' under lattice operations.

Purpose: to delimit which axioms (the conditions labelled S... and L... on the previous page) a 'support' formalism for a combinatorial or tame analysis situs can satisfy. Concretely, it shows that the support map can be compatible with neither the lattice operations nor distributivity once 'open' is taken in this formal sense.
errors: B_z is described as {z' : z'<z or z'>z}, the comparable elements, but it is called the complement of A_z = {z}. The literal complement of {z} also contains the incomparable elements, so the notation is loose: B_z seems to be the union of the closed 'droites', not the full set-theoretic complement.
'|B_z| = J \ |z|' mixes spaces: |z| lives in I ⊔ I', so presumably (I ⊔ I') \ |z| is meant.

Next page: the example (with 0 as bottom and z3 ≤ A_{z1}∨A_{z2}) shows failure of distributivity. Failure of modularity would require a pair with A_{z3} ≤ A_{z1}, which is not exhibited here. Grothendieck hedges with 'ou distributivité'.

Since the opens form a non-distributive lattice, 'ouvert' cannot mean an open set of an ordinary topology, whose opens form a distributive frame. It must be a formal open in his axiomatic structure; the page does not spell this out.

ideas.what: Product of two bounded chains I×I' with adjoined 0,1 as a model of the space of 'liens' on a two-strand string (a circle)
ideas.modern_name: poset of contractible subcomplexes / product order on intervals

ideas.what: Support map from figures/strata to an underlying point set, and the test of its compatibility with lattice sup/inf
ideas.modern_name: support map; lattice homomorphism to power set
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to tame topology programme in Esquisse d'un programme §5, but not this formalism

ideas.what: Counterexample: supports fail to commute with ∧ and ∨, and the lattice of 'opens' is non-distributive
ideas.modern_name: non-distributive lattice of formal opens (vs. frames being distributive)

missed.claim: An axiomatic 'analysis situs' is being built from compact contractible 'liens' with a support map, in which the opens form a lattice that need not be distributive. This page fixes limits on its axioms; the resulting framework was never published.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mild interest for the history of Grothendieck's tame-topology programme. The counterexample itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but elementary counterexample within an unpublished axiomatic framework. It documents the 1986 Analysis situs effort, but the mathematics (product of chains, non-distributivity) is routine.
transcription_corrections: 'Si pour trouver J' is likely 'soit pour trouver J' or 'd'où un truc J'; the sense is the definition of J with J° = I×I'.
'[-J_{z''}-]' is crossed out before [z'',1]; 'droites' is written over the crossed-out 'petits'.
'à valeurs dans I ⊔ I' ... si z={x,x'}': read z=(x,x') with x∈I, x'∈I'.
'comme il se doit' is preceded by 'comme il se doit' in the margin, and 'Mais si z1, z2 ne sont pas comparables' is correct.
In the final line the second interval is written [x'2,x'1] (with the I' order reversed), consistent with the figure.
